Answer: B
Reason: The chest X-ray (Figure 6) demonstrates a small right hemithorax with opacity and ipsilateral mediastinal shift (dextroposition of the heart), while the CT images (Figures 4 and 5) reveal an anomalous venous structure (red arrows) draining into the inferior vena cava/right atrium region. These findings are classic for Scimitar syndrome (hypogenetic lung syndrome), which involves right lung hypoplasia/aplasia and partial anomalous pulmonary venous return.
